description: Shows your code running, visually, while you debug, to teach programming. Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python and any language with a debugger in VS Code.
view.name: Visualization
config.beginnerMode: Shows a sentence explaining what changed in each step.
config.animationSpeed.slow: Movements take twice as long, good for presenting or recording the screen.
config.animationSpeed.fast: Half the duration, for those who step quickly with F10.
config.animationSpeed.off: No movement; changes are still highlighted.
config.animationSpeed.slow.label: Slow
config.animationSpeed.normal.label: Normal
config.animationSpeed.fast.label: Fast
config.animationSpeed.off.label: Off
config.maxElements: How many positions of each array are read and drawn.
config.valueNames: Names of integer variables that hold a value, not a position. They do not become arrows under the arrays.
config.revealOnDebug: Opens the Code Scope panel on the first stop of each debug session.
config.pauseOnErrors: Pauses the program on errors that nobody handles (uncaught exceptions), so the panel can show where and why it broke.
command.present: Presentation mode (large panel next to the code)
walkthrough.title: Get started with Code Scope
walkthrough.description: See your code run: the panel draws arrays, lists, stacks, objects and recursion while you debug.
walkthrough.sample.title: Open a sample
walkthrough.sample.description:
Start with a ready program in Java, JavaScript or Python. The sample is copied to a folder you pick, with everything needed to debug it.
[Open a sample](command:codeScope.openSample)
Java needs the [Extension Pack for Java](command:workbench.extensions.search?%22vscjava.vscode-java-pack%22) and a JDK; Python needs the [Python extension](command:workbench.extensions.search?%22ms-python.python%22). JavaScript only needs Node.js 22 or newer.
walkthrough.sample.alt: The Code Scope panel showing a list that gains an item in the middle.
walkthrough.step.title: Put a breakpoint and press F10
walkthrough.step.description:
Open BubbleSort (bubbleSort.js, bubble_sort.py), click left of the line number the comment points to, and start debugging with F5. Each F10 runs one line: the panel animates what changed and says it in plain words.
[Show the panel](command:codeScope.show)
walkthrough.step.alt: Bubble sort in the panel: two boxes swap places while i and j move under the array.
walkthrough.more.title: Guess, present, save
walkthrough.more.description:
**Guess first** asks what a variable will hold before the line runs. **Presentation mode** opens a large panel next to the code, for class or a screen recording. **Save image** turns the step into a PNG for slides.
[Presentation mode](command:codeScope.present)
